function.name: submit_plan
function.description:
Submit the whole plan at once: the steps in order. Nothing runs until the user approves it. A step that makes a new layer (buffer, count_in, find_where, keep_inside, remove_inside, split_parts, summarize_each) is referred to by later steps as "#k" (k = its position, from 1). Steps:
- count_in(points, areas, stat?, field?): Count points in each area of an area layer, or take a statistic of a numeric point field per area (stat sum|mean|median|min|max with field, e.g. total students per district: stat 'sum', field 'students'). New layer: the areas with a count field named after the counted layer: its name in lower case when the name is one to three plain words (Schools: 'schools'; World cities: 'world cities'), otherwise 'points', 'lines' or 'areas' (storm_tracks_1980-2026: 'lines'); later steps can always name it '#k'. With a statistic, the field is '<stat> <field>' ('sum students', 'mean students', 'median students', 'minimum students', 'maximum students'). It counts any layer's objects: areas (islands, lakes) count by a point inside each; lines (storm tracks, rivers, roads) count once in every area they cross or touch. To count what lies near each point (islands within 100 km of each city), first buffer the points with merge false, then count_in(points=<the layer to count>, areas='#k').
- count_here(points, area): Count points inside one area (a selected, named or drawn area).
- which_container(point, areas): Which area (of an area layer) one point is in.
- whats_inside(area, layer): Show the objects of a layer that lie inside one area (lists them). Not for counting per area.
- summarize_data_here(area, layer): How many of a layer's objects lie inside one area, their total area in km² (measured from the shapes) or total length, and each number field's total, mean and range (the total area of the walled cities in Shandong).
- buffer(layer, object?, merge?, distance): The area within a distance of a whole layer, or of one object of it (give object: a named object, or {layer} alone for the selected object). New area layer. merge false keeps each object's buffer separate.
- measure_area(area): Measure one area object (geodesic).
- measure_length(line): Measure one line object (geodesic).
- summarize_each(raster, areas, band?, stat?): Summarize a raster in each area of an area layer. New layer: the areas with fields '<raster> mean', '<raster> median', '<raster> minimum', '<raster> maximum', '<raster> sum', '<raster> std dev' (Heat: 'Heat mean'); stat picks the headline (default mean). A category raster (e.g. land cover) gives each class's share of every area instead.
- summarize_here(raster, area, band?, stat?): Summarize a raster inside one area (stat default mean). A category raster gives class shares.
- summarize_drawn(raster, area?, band?, stat?): Summarize a raster in an area the user will draw (omit area), or in a drawn area.
- summarize_over_time(raster, place, band?, order?): A raster with a time slider (NetCDF) at one place on every time step: the area's average, or the value under a point, for each day or month, ranked highest first (order 'lowest': lowest first). Answers the hottest day in a place, the wettest month, how a value changed over time. Only the raster's shown time step is used by every other raster action.
- add_raster_values(raster, points, band?): Add the raster's value at each (shown) point as a field named after the raster (Heat: 'Heat'); hidden points stay blank. Changes the points layer; no new layer.
- rank_by_value(layer, order?, field): Rank a layer's objects by a numeric field: highest first, or with order 'lowest' lowest first (the coldest, smallest, fewest, lowest).
- calculate_field(layer, first, op, second, name?): Add a number field calculated from two values: first (a number field) op (add|subtract|multiply|divide) second (a number field or a number), e.g. density = population divide area_km2. Blank inputs or division by zero give blanks. Adds the field 'name' (default 'first op second') to the layer; no new layer.
- split_parts(layer): Split a line or area layer's multi-part features into one feature per part (e.g. separate islands). New layer with a 'part' field.
- find_where(raster, conditions?): Find the areas where every raster condition holds (e.g. elevation at least 3000 and rainfall at least 500). raster: the first raster; conditions: [{field: <raster name>, op: at_least | at_most | between, value, value2}] in the raster's unit. New area layer, one area per connected group of cells, largest first, with fields name, area_km2, cells and '<raster> mean'.
- keep_inside(layer, areas): Keep only the part of a layer inside an area layer's (shown) areas (clip). New layer with the same fields (an area_km2 field is copied, not recomputed).
- remove_inside(layer, areas): Remove the part of a layer inside an area layer's (shown) areas (erase; 'away from', 'outside'). New layer with the same fields.
- nearest_distance(layer, other): Add to each object of a layer the geodesic distance in km to the nearest (shown) object of another layer (other), and that object's name. Adds fields 'km to nearest <other>' and 'nearest <other>', <other> being the other layer's name in the singular and lower case when it is one to three plain words (Rivers: 'km to nearest river'; World cities: 'km to nearest world city'), otherwise 'point', 'line' or 'area'; later steps can name the distance '#k'. Changes the layer; no new layer.
- nearest_other(layer): Add to each object the distance in km to the nearest other object of the same layer (isolation), and its name: fields 'km to nearest other <layer, singular>' ('km to nearest other hospital'). Only the objects the layer shows count as others: filter first to measure among some of them (the M8+ quakes among themselves); with one object shown, every other object counts. Changes the layer; no new layer.
- join_by_location(layer, areas): Add to each object of a layer the fields of the area it lies in (spatial join; lines and areas use a point on them): layer, areas, fields (comma list of the areas' fields; all by default). The new fields keep the areas' field names. Changes the layer; no new layer.
- add_measurements(layer): Add area_km2 and perimeter_km (areas), length_km (lines), and longitude and latitude (degrees, of a point on each object) as fields. A field name the layer already has gets ' 2' (area_km2 2). Changes the layer; no new layer.
- match_table(layer, table, layer_field?, table_field?, repeats?): Add a table's columns (a table without locations, e.g. statistics by district) to a layer by a key both share: layer, table, layer_field and table_field (the key columns; they may have different names, e.g. 'name' and 'district'; left out, the best pair is found), repeats (latest | combine | auto) for several rows per object. The new fields keep the table's names. Changes the layer; no new layer.
- filter(layer, conditions): show only objects meeting all conditions (it replaces the layer's earlier filter, so repeat earlier conditions to keep them); changes the layer, no new layer. Ops: is, is_not, contains, starts_with, ends_with, is_empty, above (>), below (<), at_least (>=), at_most (<=), between (inclusive), before, after, any_of.
- color_by(layer, field) / view_data(layer) / zoom_to(layer, field?, value?): only when asked for.
- ask_user(question, choices?): one question, only when needed. Alone in the plan.
- cannot_do(reason): the tools can't answer. Alone in the plan.

points.description: count_in: the layer to count (points; areas, e.g. islands, by a point inside each; lines, e.g. storm tracks, once in every area they cross); add_raster_values: a point layer

point.description: One object: {layer, field, value} with value as stored (resolve_feature finds it); omit field and value for the selected object, a drawn area, or the layer's only shown object.

line.description: One object: {layer, field, value} with value as stored (resolve_feature finds it); omit field and value for the selected object, a drawn area, or the layer's only shown object.

area.description: One object: {layer, field, value} with value as stored (resolve_feature finds it); omit field and value for the selected object, a drawn area, or the layer's only shown object.

place.description: summarize_over_time: one area or point. One object: {layer, field, value} with value as stored (resolve_feature finds it); omit field and value for the selected object, a drawn area, or the layer's only shown object.

object.description: One object: {layer, field, value} with value as stored (resolve_feature finds it); omit field and value for the selected object, a drawn area, or the layer's only shown object. Optional.

distance.description: number and unit: '500 m', '2 km', '3 mi', '100 ft'

order.description: rank_by_value, summarize_over_time: highest first (default) or lowest first

other.description: nearest_distance: the layer to measure to

fields.description: join_by_location: comma list of the areas' fields to add (all by default)

table.description: match_table: the table to add to the layer

layer_field.description: match_table: the layer's key column (found automatically when left out)

table_field.description: match_table: the table's key column; it may have another name than the layer's

repeats.description: match_table: several table rows for one object: latest (by a year or date column) or combine (counts summed, other numbers averaged); auto picks

first.description: calculate_field: the first value, a number field of the layer (first op second)

second.description: calculate_field: the second value, a number field or a number

value.description: number (in the field's unit) or a stored text/category value

function.name: resolve_feature
function.description: Look up how a layer stores a name or category the user wrote (another language, abbreviation, nickname): returns up to 5 stored values with their field. A lookup, not a plan step; it doesn't take a step number.
